title: Easy to set up
text: It works well once set up and the setup is easy. The application software is a little annoying in one respect: the camera views on my iPad are always rotated to portrait orientation, which makes the view itself sideways instead of vertical. I assume that it's some configuration issue, but I can't find it: it shouldn't be that obscure to find.The basic functions (detection, control) are mostly fine. You will need to subscribe to the PLUS service from WYZE in order to have longer recordings made after motion detection, to control the rest period between recordings, and to detect anything other than motion. It's not expensive, but if you're on a tight budget, you should check the current subscription price, too. The battery charge lasts several weeks in our rural location, with only two or three callers a day (UPS and Post Office, mostly).You'll also need to buy little memory cards for the camera(s) and the base station, if you want the videos quickly available for review and you don't have fast internet speeds. I bought mine directly from WYZE to assure they'd work, other reviewers have said that they've had problems with non-WYZE supplied cards. The cards don't fill up fast (good compression, I guess) and allow you to keep the videos for longer than WYZE will keep them for you.Detection of motion is not as quick as I'd like, particularly at night. It misses our newspaper delivery which takes about 5 seconds for the carrier to drive into our driveway, drop the paper, then back out. There may be a sensitivity control to adjust in the application; if so, I've clearly missed it. It did detect a bobcat at night that jumped onto and walked along the top of our gate, so it's not clear to me what is going on with detection sensitivity -- see a bobcat, miss a car?WYZE keeps making improvements to the software for the camera system; we've had about three updates from them since late 2020, when I bought and installed this. As one would hope, the camera system recovers from an electric blackout quite nicely. The cameras seem nicely weather resistant, too; we've had some heavy downpours and wind this winter.

text: [[VIDEOID:7ae975dde0e13eb7fa2312200aa2ccc7]] Not everyone can afford a 'Surface'. Not everyone NEEDS a surface. I have a work computer, a personal computer and a tablet. My personal laptop is BIG. I don't like lugging it around all the time, because of it's size and weight. But, I do like having that technology with me for all the same reasons I have the laptop. So, a nice lightweight tablet with a detachable keyboard folio cover is the answer. And, EOSO has the best one at the best price. The keyboard is almost as big as the one on my Dell Latitude 7490 (the work computer) and just as easy to use. the keystroke is very comfortable. The ABS keys are very durable. It's a full function keyboard. Not the basic type that is so common. It works with iOS, Windows and Android. It's super easy to pair. Will work with ANY tablet from 9 to 10.5 inches. The tablet is held securely in place. The keyboard is easily removed for comfort. The battery life is phenomenal. This device makes life so much easier. I could not be happier. The only problem I have found, as I continue to work with this keyboard / folio is that the keyboard does NOT have a standby or sleep mode, where it will automatically 'hibernate' after so many minutes of NOT being used. So, after a day or so of being idle, the battery dies. Not really a deal breaker. I can just charge it or remember to shut it off, when I'm not using it. But, seeing that there ARE keyboards out there that DO have a 'hibernation' mode for about the same price, I had to delete one star for this particular product.

title: Fantastic look, but the interior is sideways?
text: I'm a guy and I eat cows and love their tanned hides as luggage, wallets and bags as homage to life and sustenance they provide in my life. Seriously, use everything or go vegan, and I am not a big broccoli fan. As for this exact sling bag. I really love the look, feel and smell. IT IS a big part of why I and likely you buy leather. It was a little smaller than what I thought I needed, but I have larger leather backpack for the heavy bulky stuff. The build is great and the zippers all move well. What I guess I didn't get my head around was the interior and the angle of the divided sections. Great when you set it lengthwise on table or desk to fill the main compartment with the items you want to take (like you do with any bag or even a purse). But, when you have it loaded and toss it on a shoulder and go. Everything in the main section is now at 90 degrees and many smaller items fall to the bottom. I might have chosen a bit differently had I realized that. Still love the bag and I have adapted to the minor quirk for me. Just didn't have that flaw of this or all "sling bags" in mind ahead of purchase. You see the orientation as a small backpack in the photos and that's how my, man eat cow brain thought it would be with stuff inside, despite the interior pics.I would likely buy this again if I ever needed another man purse (as wife calls it) or small backpack, just wanted to share for others who might have missed how the bags orientation alters from the reality of actually carrying the bag. Also note that for shorter folks, the strap is pretty long even at its shortest length. I'm just under 6ft and this rides top to mid rear pocket of my pants when pants are worn like a grown up. Sling length diagonally puts it where most backpacks lay in mid to lower back above the belt.As for filling. I tend to have a camera/camcorder or even a DJI mini pro 3 with screen controller inside. Everything rides pretty good. Just be proactive for the small items that might shift and be on the bottom of the main section. Stuff like screens from electronics may get scuffed or worse should something rough transfers on your journey. At least you have more pockets with traditional less gravity challenged orientations available.

text: I bought this EVGA CLC 280/280mm AIO a few months ago but I wanted to try it out for a while before I left a review to really get a chance to see how it performs over a longer period of time.Firstly, I am running this AIO on an i7 8700K WITH an overclock of 5GHz on all cores. With this AIO my idle temperatures are in the mid to high 20C range and under full load it warms up to the low to mid 80s C. This is great performance for such a high overclock. With stock clock speeds this AIO should perform much better and shouldn’t go above 65C during full loads.Secondly, I want to share my experience with EVGA’s superb customer service. When I installed this AIO I had a problem with the RGB not working. I tried reinstalling it, using different motherboard plugins for the cables, but nothing seemed to fix it. Finally I contacted EVGA by email. They mentioned that the USB cable could be defective. Here is what amazes me: EVGA sent me a brand new USB cable at no cost to myself and they didn’t even make me go through the hoops and hassle of sending my product back, paying for shipping, waiting for processing, etc., they just sent me a brand new cable and THEY paid to have it shipped. I got it 2 days later.That is the kind of customer service I love and is the reason I try to buy EVGA products when possible. Most companies will not do that. They’ll put you through the hassle of many steps and lots of waiting around and processing which discourages a lot of customers, such as myself, from even bothering to contact them when something goes wrong.All in all, a great product with even better customer service!Thank you EVGA!

title: Take a Hike and Enjoy the Natural Scenery
text: Among my means of physical fitness, the one I partake in with the greatest level of frequency is walking. If nothing else, I will take a quick jaunt around the block but what I love best is a lengthy hike through a natural area. Living in the large metropolitan area of Houston, these natural areas do exist and many of them make for a great morning or afternoon away from the noise and chaos of the city. And an excellent guide that brings it all together is 60 Hikes within 60 Milles, Houston.The 60 featured hikes in this book are sorted by region and numbered from 1 to 60, for easy future reference. With each hike, the reader is presented with the name of the actual trail, its location, a description, and nearby activities. There is a quick fact list that lets you know what to expect in terms of scenery, what the traffic is like, the facilities you will find, a contact phone number and website, and other useful things to make your hiking adventure the best, most efficient it can possibly be. There are even GPS coordinates to help you pinpoint the exact location and a map for guidance.I have taken about 15 of the 60 hikes in this book and I really enjoy how the book describes each trail and what to expect. It provides lots and lots of details, from the signage you can expect to see along the way to the sometimes interesting wildlife you may encounter, like alligators and snakes. I like the additional tips provided in the description, like where you will find the best views, where restrooms are located, and much more. The book is all about guidance and it wants your hike to be the best, most frustration- free hike possible.The quality of this book is top- notch and you realize this immediately, before you even open the pages. The reason I say this is because the book is heavier than expected and you just know with weight like that, it is certain to be printed on high quality paper. And it most definitely is- the heavy weight, glossy paper means easy to read maps and colorful pictures are right at your fingertips.I love taking a good hike and with 60 Hikes within 60 Miles, Houston I have a guide that I can use for future adventure and exercise. From the marshy areas of the National Wildlife Refuges to the paved walkways along the bayous, this book is ready to help satisfy your hunger for a good hike in the greater Houston area. It’s an excellent book that earns an enthusiastic five stars from me!

text: I know that this book is about teenagers. I know from reading the back that its about noble teens in a magical academy and their final passage into adulthood.That doesn't excuse the angst from the main character. I HATE angst. Its not heroic, its not fun and quite frankly so many authors use it as a substitute for real plot and character development that I passionately despise its use.And of course, in this book the main character seems to have all sorts of uncertainty. He has a betrothed (who doesn't really appear in this book sadly). And he worries about the betrothal (not sure why, it doesn't play a role in this book at all really). He has his twin sister who is locked away due to previous actions. (although she gets a cameo that I'll admit was well thought out.) And he has cousins determined to ruin his last year at school through their hijinks. But the big one is his father forcing him to participate in a Challenge.This series has all been mini/partial mysteries with much of the "action" being more discovery of plots and treasons. No one is who he is portrayed and there have been far too many backstabbings and betrayals than there has been good action and serious character development.Its not a bad book, and I will admit to enjoying it once I gave up on the author not thrusting the angst level to infinity and beyond. But there are many quirks that reduced my enjoyment. I'll give it 3 stars.

title: Genuine GM Replacement Part
text: In 2019, the button on my original part started getting "loose" and I was AFRAID that it was going to bust, leaving me no way to "shift" from park/reverse/drive ... etc. Yes, it is an automatic, but you get the idea of moving it into and out of the gears.I finally got some extra money and decided to order this part. Then, not feeling too "car savvy" ... I wanted to see how much a dealership would charge. As a woman, car maintenance and repairs are not my thing. Just last year I managed to do the third brake light bulbs.Today (3/29/2020), I got the part and decided to run some errands. And, the button on my old was way too loose for me. Honestly, I was a bit worried. After getting home, and still pondering if I should call the dealership tomorrow (3/30 - Monday), I decided to look up videos on how to change it out. Not having the money to correct anything should it go wrong, yes I was hesitant.After backing my car out of the garage (as I had little room to do what I needed to do with the car door open), I did what I was instructed to do:1. Start car2. Shift into NeutralNow, I wasn't told to turn off the car, but I did. Since the parking brake doesn't work on my car, and I'm lucky enough to have a "steep" curb up into the garage, I decided to "straddle" the curb. Back end out, front in. That worked.And, I installed this part myself. Yes, getting the silver part unlocked was tricky. After that? I used the tiny hex/Allen wrench/key to unscrew the old lever handle. Off it came. I then popped on the new part. Screwed it in, screwed the silver part in place. Started the car ... and no issue with the button!As I purchased the extended warranty, I'm feeling pretty safe now. And, with it being a genuine GM part, I'm definitely feeling good about this.

title: Great value for the money, works with Sony WF-1000XM3
text: As I am sure is the case with many, I purchased this after seeing it listed by the New York Times in their portable BT transmitter review list. It was bought specifically to allow me to transmit BT audio from my computer to my Sony WF-1000XM3 earbuds. As the Sony earbuds only support SBC with these, I wasn't expecting stellar audio quality - I usually use them for lectures or podcast-like content, or for fairly low-bitrate music anyway. I wanted to see if the advantages of true-wireless earbuds were worth the sacrifice in quality before I invested in a more expensive BT transmitter and BT receiver+high-end IEMs. As such, I do not use the receive function, and I do not use the battery on the unit - it is always plugged in via USB. I did briefly test the battery though and can confirm it lasts at least 30m.Note: I went with this type unit, instead of USB, because I wanted to have the ability to test it in multiple environments, including while running and in the car for single-ear usage. Normally, I'd go with a USB solution for computer use in order to avoid the conversion of the audio from to and back from analog.Initial SetupDead simple - I connected the Line Out on my computer to the input on the transmitter, and alternately, the HP out on my stereo receiver to the input on the transmitter. I also tried it with a Sansa Clip+ MP3 player. It worked in all cases, though with the WF-1000XM3 I had to keep the input volume on the BT transmitter under 30% and allow the headphones to do the real amplification, as otherwise the audio would distort.BT SetupFairly simple. I put my earbuds into pairing mode, the transmitter into pairing mode, and they connected within 10s. Afterward, they maintained their connection for the most part, I've had to re-pair a couple times over the last three weeks, but that is mostly a learning curve. Re-pairing is easy - just hold the pairing button down for two seconds and place the receiving device in pairing mode.RangeUnpredictable, and sensitive. If the transmitter is located on a desk, at least twelve inches away from other electronics, then the range is remarkable. I can leave the room, pass through the adjacent room, and enter into the next room - a total of maybe thirty feet, through two or three walls - and start to lose audio at the end. This is despite being only five feet from a wireless router. However, if I move the transmitter six inches over so it is next to my monitor, or a couple feet so that it is within three feet of the router, the earbuds will begin to drop out even at ten feet. So it is very sensitive to environment.Audio QualityDecent. Better than I expected, but I haven't used bluetooth audio in ten years. It can be hard to really gauge it, because the Sony WF-1000XM3 are true wireless earbuds and I can't A/B test them to compare BT quality to a cable. I would say that the BT audio quality is equivalent to that produced when my Sony earbuds are connected to my smartphone. While it is decent, it can't compare to wired earbuds of even fairly middling quality. You lose highs and lows. For dialogue content, lectures and the like, no issue.SummarySeems to be a great entry-level transmitter for the average consumer. I'm glad I bought it, because it is reliable and easy to use, and has shown me that the freedom of using wireless earbuds is definitely worth the hit to quality - I can always use my full circumaural headphones if I want to watch a movie or listen critically. Would recommend.

title: What was the Cassus Belli?
text: I might have spelt the title wrong. But having played too much Crusader Kings 2 and even some CK3, I find myself asking "why" whenever a fantasy world has nations go to war. And in this tale that definitely became a concern.Of course, the story starts with an orphan watching 2 wizards fight to the death and somehow absorbing the power from both as they die. This makes him far more powerful than most wizards, but at first he just makes a haven for himself in a secluded alley in the city he lived in (which happens to be a nation's capitol.)The story builds from there as our hero becomes powerful enough to drive the story to new heights and to get involved in the nation's troubles and issues.Which is where I start shaking my head. Like just about every story of this type the neighboring kingdoms have huge armies and they want to take over this struggling kingdom. But there is no real "reason" given. The kingdom has a rather unpleasant royal family but they do have a clear line of succession which means no nearby nation can claim they are attacking to put X on the throne. And neither neighbor is claiming imperial dominion. Its like "We'll take this kingdom for "reasons"". Which leaves me wondering, especially since 2 different kingdoms try individually. It was like the nation was just "weak", but then was there any gain to be made? How many kingdoms can afford to conquer and garrison a kingdom that doesn't give them massive amount of loot?But that's me. I get lost in questions like that. The story itself is fairly good, although the MC is far too powerful and surprisingly well read for a street rat. (but that is explained with a bit of hand-wavium)Not bad, but the flaws leave me unable to give it 4 stars. Its worth the read if you can turn off any need for the world politics to make sense.

title: Enjoyable Juvenile Mystery Featuring Cree Cousins
text: Did you ever wish someone would bring back those good old fashioned kids' mysteries, like the Happy Hollisters, but with more diverse protagonists? Well, you've found your series. The Mighty Muskrats are four cousins who live on the Windy Lake Reserve in Canada: Chickadee, the only girl; Otter, an orphan raised by Chickadee's grandfather; and brothers Atim and Samuel. The local mining company has hired the required archaeologist—so that no Native artifacts or remains are disturbed—but he's disappeared, the only clue his boat found grounded on an island. The children's Uncle Levi, head of the Windy Lake police, is teaming with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police to find him. The Muskrats vow to do it themselves. In a parallel plot, the kids' cousin Denice is heading up a group of activists at the mining company who say they are not following regulations and are polluting the lake. To make her point, Denice chains herself to a mooring post on the company's pier, and the angry owner wants her gone, but he is told she isn't blocking anything and she has a right to protest. The children's grandfather says she is on a vision quest and must complete it.The story is a satisfying mix of mystery, old-fashioned kids' adventure elements like a clubhouse, and elements of the tribal culture at Windy Lake, including the method of tracking down the missing archaeologist and Denice's willingness to fight for her people's way of life and environment.My only quibble with the book is that there are too many instances of Atim flicking his head (to keep his hair out of his eyes). It just keeps coming up in the text too many times.

It's pronounced "fry-nee". Ugh. (2) She turns Countess Lieven (a real historical person) into Princess Lieven, when just copying from Heyer would have avoided this error; it doesn't even require original research! Ugh.Yes, I'm a picker of nits. But I did enjoy the book, it's a nice light bit of fluff for when you're in the mood (and are willing to let Heyer competitors meet a lower standard).

text: This product description doesn't do this product justice. I am impressed. I am already a fan of Sanag products, so I expected this to be good. It is. I'll list everything I can think of below.I have been looking for an easy to use fitness watch for my 70+ years old mom. She mentioned interest in one, but I am not sure how much she will enjoy it. While I like fitbit (been using that brand since 2015) I didnt want to get her one if she wouldnt like the technology. I looked through what I already own, but nothing seemed right. I have a garmin that I wouldnt have anyone new to fitness watches use (hate that thing). I have an Amazon Halo, which is great but its attached to my account so I cant have her try it. And I have a weird off brand tracker that I got a few years ago that it too complicated to use (clunky app, slow to respond swiping). I basically need a tracker to be easy to use (both the tracker and the app) and be something I feel comfortable having my tech adverse mom use. I chose this based on what I read in the description AND my positive experience so far with Sanag.I figured I would try this watch for a couple of weeks before deciding if it would work for her. I have been wearing it day and night for a little over a week, and I may not give it to her.. because I love it. hahaI'm just going to bullet point the features I have noticed so far:--waterproof. I wear it 24/7. Though I do take off for showering, I am just used to doing that. I also clean homes for living, and this can take a beating.-- easy to find, install, and use App (da fit), many customizations, options to set up.--pairs easily with bluetooth; no hassle.--interesting color, nice feeling band. Very secure feeling. Though, I'd prefer the band to be a little longer. I have a 7" wrist, and this just fits. Will be fine for my mom who has very petite bone structure.--super long battery life. I charge my fitbit sense every other day. Other than initial charge, I have not yet had to charge this. I'd say they are accurate on their 7-14 day charge on normal use, or 30 days on standby. That being said..-- blood O2 measurment is on demand. Not automatic. Just go into watch face or app to measure. It keeps track. Heart rate can be continuous measurement or on demand.--Can choose from many many many watch faces. So many different styles, some are super cute. Different faces depending on what you want to see, ie just the time, time and date, time, date, steps, hr, cals burned, etc. If you have a few that you like, then you can scroll through what you have used in your watch itself to to select one, or you can go to the app to select one.--steps are accurate as far as side by side with my Fit bit Sense. Same steps (within 20 steps) when worn side by side on same wrist.--gorgeous display- very colorful and easy to read--easy to navigate with swiping; very responsive. Easy to back out from selections.--on watch can see time, date, steps, heart rate, 02, blood pressure (havent checked yet for accuracy but I will), weather, sleep data, exercise specific date (and tracking), alarms, timers, music control, camera shutter control, and settings notifications (can set up to see notifications from many sources such as email, phone calls, texts, FB, IG, Whatsapp, etc etc ect-- huge list that can be turned on for notifications to allow to come through if you want. Can pick and choose).--on watch can select options such as "do not disturb", brightness settings, lock option,--can connect to google fit--can keep track of other health trends (menstrual, for example).--can set a step goal, reminders to move, reminders to drink waterI am not sure if there is a spot to adjust how long the face stays lit when looking at something. As of now, it goes black after a few seconds. Much like other fitness watches.--App has all this same info, with ability to look at more details--VERY easy to navigate app.REALLY an impressive gadget. I think some of it will come down to preference. I am still getting used to it, and sometimes I find the outer button is easily pressed by my bent wrist. I have accidentally changed my watch face that way, but I am seeing now that if I end up on that screen I have to make sure I am setting the face by swiping up (otherwise navigates to another face by swiping left/right). Litte annoyances that will vary.For all that it offers, for the ease of use especially compared to some name brands, I am compelled to go 5 stars. If we could do half stars, maybe 4.5. But I like it more than 4 stars. Overall nothing glaring bad or super negative comes to mind. I'll update as I learn more or think of more, or experience something different (good or bad).reasonable price at $79 (though I had a coupon which really helped make my decision), any higher and I would go with namebrand.

The cover feels amazing, with a soft texture (similar to suede) but sturdy boards. The spine uses a different, harder leather, as you'd expect from a real book. There's just a little bit of filigree decoration embossed into each outside corner, and the stitching is uniform and well-placed. It can be zipped up from either side.On top of that, it actually smells like a real book! That's one of the biggest things I miss when using an eReader, so it's nice to have it again.Overall, it's clear that the designers put a lot of thought into what makes a case pleasant but inconspicuous for the reader, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a case for their Kindle. title: Another example of the world's dumbest human being as a character
text: Good lord, another Isekai/harem tale about a barely functioning mouth breather who would lose a game of tic-tac-toe against a dog. This guy isn't just a little dumb, its very clear that if he tried to sit and chew bubblegum at the same time he'd fall out of his chair due to inattention.He's just that bloody stupid.But of course, that seems almost necessary as once again he's more powerful than the entirety of the Norse Pantheon as a group. He could defeat Superman with just his pinky. Well at least that's implied constantly without there being any good reason to back that up.Yes, I'm bashing this book. One thing that I desperately want the authors of these Isekai/harem tales to do is twofold.First, smarten up the main characters. Stop with the guys who do beyond stupid things without thinking about what might happen. In this book after already getting sent to a new world because he touched an object in a room he had been repeatedly told not to enter. [and I won't get into the stupidity of his janitorial job at an archeological site, that's a whole different idiocy that this author inserted.] But after that, and having multiple people get on his case for things that the person in the body he was swapped into did before he arrived, he then attempts a magic spell without having any idea what it might do. In a crowded cafeteria. Using a magic source that he had no training in using.Can we say massive disaster?And that brings up the second major issue with this and so many other Isekai/harem tales. Why is this guy so bloody powerful. I put in a recent review that part of why people like a movie like Die Hard isn't that John McClane is some uber-human capable of great feats. instead he's an everyman who struggles and is bloodied throughout the movie, but in the end is able to win thanks to grit, determination and a little bit of luck. Here, the main character Jake shows no grit or determination, and his successes seem to be based on the fact that he's got access to so much power that he'd have to try to fail.And I hate to say it but that's boring beyond belief. This guy isn't going to have challenges to meet, but some speed bump type obstacles and then the clothing will go flying. Its readable, but its nothing that I really enjoy or find interesting.And yet, I keep trying out stories in this genre, because the few good ones are amazing. Sadly, this tale and author are one and done for me. His inability to break from the trend of poorly written Mary Sue type characters who are stupider than your average worm and yet more powerful than they need to be just left me saying. "I read it."I give it 3 stars for being decently edited and flowing fairly well, but I'd say that unless you like the genre, its not worth your time.

title: You get what you pay for ...
text: In the space of 18 months, I went from active world traveler to severely mobility challenged due to some significant health events. I've always been fiercely independent, so asking for help is extremely difficult for me. But the reality is that I can no longer move around like I used to -- I need "aids" to do even the simplest tasks.While I was recovering in a skilled nursing facility, the occupational and physical therapists recommended getting a rollator (as opposed to a walker) to help me get around easier. Due to my "heft" (ahem!), I wanted to get the sturdiest one I could find.First stop: AmazonAnd here it is. I've actually had this unit since November 2020, using it multiple times a day. It's sturdy, comes already assembled, and does everything I need it to do. It has metal wheels (NOT plastic), and a strong frame. The included bag holds a lot, too.I'm currently living in an assisted living facility and this allows me to get around, participate in activities, gather mail and packages from the incoming mail area -- basically, everything I need to function daily. I use our local "paratransit" service, which uses a lift for folks like me who can no longer deal with stairs -- and I just roll onto the platform with my rollator and board the bus easily.When I want to go out with friends, I do need to make sure their vehicle has space for this. I have a very bad shoulder, so I also wanted something that didn't weigh a lot. This weighs about 11 lbs -- and it folds easily (just lift up on the handle in the seat). Once folded, I can usually get it into the trunk of a friend's car without any problems. But it definitely won't fit in a small compact car trunk -- you need more like a mid-size car or SUV or minivan. So keep that in mind if this is something you'll need to transport frequently.Like I said, early 18 months of almost constant use -- around my apartment, around the building, in and out of various vehicles -- and it is showing no signs of wear.Seriously, since my health issues arrived, this has been my best investment in terms of "aids" that actually do make my life more livable. Highly recommended.

text: Suzanne Venker believes that men and women have different needs, expectations and desires. This is very obvious even from a very casual look at how the world is in reality. Women often get emotionally attached to men who just want a temporary relationship. This is a problem for women who want to start a family and build a solid long-term relationship. What is a woman to do?Any woman who dedicated years to a relationship only to find out the guy really didn't want to get married will relate to this book. It happened to me ( I dated a man for four years during my college years and he even gave me a promise ring) and it happens to a lot of women who are single now and nearing the end of their fertile years. Luckily I met someone else and got married at 27 and eventually decided the first man I wanted to marry was really not that interesting. :) I live and learn. I'll have been married for 25 years in a few days so was looking for a book on the subject of marriage.What I did like about this book is the straight talk about dating that women who want to get married desperately need to know. However I did not think the authors went far enough. Even if you are engaged to be married and put out you have no guarantee that the man will not pull out of the relationship the day before the wedding. Men think of women as conquests at times and it is wise to understand that a man can lose interest once the conquest is over.This book is really for women who want a husband and children first and want to have a career second. Of course there are many women who are going to decide that career comes first for a while and they will wait to have kids. The problem then is that women have fertility issues at some point and it can be very expensive to get pregnant. So the author of this book presents a strong warning to women that if they make certain decisions, they may miss out on motherhood.I myself decided not to have children and I feel it was the right path for me as I've dedicated my life to other pursuits which have helped people. But I will admit that now that I'm past 50 I do see my friends enjoying visiting their grandchildren and I think I am missing out on something wonderfully loving. So I think some of this book is correct in that you can regret not having children.On the other hand I can't imagine the world without dedicated female nurses or what about secretaries who help run businesses which benefit the public or all the caring female doctors who spend their time on healing people of terrible illnesses? I think women have to make a choice early on how their life is going to be. Of course there are ways to manage working and having a family. Women do it all the time. You just have to hire help or marry a man who is willing to participate more!So if you are on the fence about what you want to do in life, this book will at least show you the options you have and give you a lot of things to consider. I did not agree with everything but a lot of the dating advice is great for women who want a man to commit. Women have much more power than they realize!~The Rebecca Review

text: Holy crap, where have I been that I hadn't read this author before (except when she co-authors with my number one Linda Howard)?I know a lot of people will pick this up and think, oh goody a shifter book. Not quite and if that's what you are looking for, you'll probably be disappointed. This is like Cinderella meets the Wicked Witch of the North, and throw in a few jokes and comic characters to break it all up. I loved it. I sat when I should have been doing a dozen other things, and read it straight through.The characters, in this book, didn't have to be developed too deeply, because it was the present day actions that formed the book. There wasn't any real backstory to speak of, but there didn't need to be (yes, I really said that. Me, yes me, who always looks for deep character development and a big, heavy duty backstory). I didn't miss any of that in this book, I was too taken with the town of Mystic Springs with its hardware store where you don't have to ask for what you want, and the restaurant where everything tastes like your favorites, and the bakery where nothing has calories (yes, I could definitely get into that). On top of a great book, I also enjoy reading her posts on social media, her humor is understated and connects with the real world.This book was a cross between a shifter story, a fantasy story, and a fairytale, all written with a strong, deft hand for fiction. I understand why some people may not like the story, and I understand that they might be disappointed that it wasn't a straight shifter story with lots of angst. title: Maladaptive Resentments and Motives for Murder at the Manor!
text: Cobblestone streets, trimmed hedgerows and top hats… Motorcars, steam engines, paneled oak, carriage houses, and mysteriously murdered squires. Deliciously sinister deeds and period-specific English countryside details fill these pages with mystery and intrigue. When letters of secret correspondence from long-lost mothers arrive (and age-old grudges resurface), repressed resentments begin to fuel dark thoughts of revenge. Disparaging remarks breed burgeoning discontent, and any family clan with considerable clout is bound to attract scandal eventually.This is the tragic tale of who stabbed the patriarch. Each and every character possesses secret vendettas and motives to kill, and it’s up to the reader to deduce who might be the true culprit of this mysterious homicide. In the spring of 1938, Chief Inspector Maxwell Hamilton and colleague, Constable Kane, are summoned to the moderately palatial estate of Hemstead Manor, an expansive red brick structure located within the small village township of St. Basil, two hours outside of London.Squire Cyril Hemstead has been found in his bed, lying gruesomely deceased with an ivory-handled carving knife in his back. Often fond of after-dinner jaunts to the local pub, he commonly returns home inebriated through the unlatched servants’ entrance. Beloved by local pub patrons for his consistent willingness to treat them all to free pints of ale, his mouth is as loose as his coin purse. As a war veteran with a great admiration for Sir Winston Churchill and tobacco, he has his own demons to fight. When the coroner coincidentally uncovers a coronary conundrum, the case quickly becomes more curiously complex.Miss Heloise Hemstead, spinster daughter of the victim, seems preternaturally detached and devoid of discernable emotion, despite her predilection to mood swings. Her mother, Dorothy, has been estranged from Cyril for the past 20 years, and as it turns out, the late old Lady Hemstead had never liked her Irish-American daughter-in-law, but she’d kept her vindictive, grand dame mouth shut tight. That is, until the day she found a way to rid the family of Dorothy’s presence by threatening to ship her off to a sanitarium in Switzerland if she didn’t leave quietly and willingly.Cora Brown, distant cousin, widow and discreet companion of the victim, provides daughter Heloise with sleeping powder on the fateful night in question, leaving no potential witnesses with clues. There are also two suspiciously reserved house servants: Ellen Kelly, devoted housekeeper and provider of scones, and Robbie Pitts, gardener, chauffeur, mechanic and temperamental handyman extraordinaire. Solicitor Cameron Philby III is the smarmy London lawyer who handles the Hemstead family assets, investments, and substantial clandestine holdings. Harry Morgan, proprietor of the local pub and old college friend of the estranged Hemstead couple, has his own dark secrets and debts to keep deeply buried.This historical fiction crime thriller is a quick and addictive read, and the entire story takes place over a period of approximately three weeks. The setting is reminiscent of a Sherlock Holmes mystery, and the layered plot with multiple suspects of interest is similar to the British film "Murder on the Orient Express". The intoxicating sense of drama and intrigue feels equal parts arsenic and lace.The lavish lifestyles are alluring, the tailored ensembles appropriately impressive, and I enjoyed seeing the conclusive epilogue that provided tidy updates at the end. This book easily receives 5 stars for being an enjoyable and well-crafted whodunit. It is “dastardly stuff, murder…” but for readers who love a good crime mystery that can be conveniently consumed in one afternoon, this tale is deliciously divine. The accusations, suspicions, and exaggerated perceptions of impropriety offer quite the guilty pleasure!

She was a normal kid being raised by her grandparents until one day they both die and suddenly she is in foster care. You go along the ride with her throughout the years as one horror show after another comes her way, and you see her personally change with every one. She has no other option but to harden herself or fall to pieces so she builds her walls. title: A helpful list
text: Often, on-line, we see sites advocating certain foods. We've to swipe over and over for maximum ad exposure. That's annoying. This book provides such a list, ad free. I wouldn't feel right were I to make a statement that eating x, y, and z results in quick weight loss without definitive proof. It might be that fish is great for that, but what about fish poached in butter at 12 oz per serving? A bibliography with up to date source material would be an asset. I like to know sources for claims. How about simplifying by calling this the Mediterranean diet? Fish, cruciferous vegetables, grapefruit, nuts, yogurt kind of for that rubric. It's nice to see warnings re mercury in larger fish and portion sizes as with nuts. Some are on special dietary plans excluding grapefruit, as GERD diet. Some avoid dairy, dut to lactose intolerance. Some avoid certain cruciferous vegetables due to stomach distress. Some eat oatmeal daily with minimal weight loss, but, possibly, better digestion or lab work results. It's difficult to quantify, since, no one has a diet plan that is verified and recorded daily. Most repeat dieters know that rapid weight loss from sticking to certain, limited foods and low quantities ends up as a springboard for a slow and steady rebound and greater weight gain. This means going back to some method that worked before, vowing to hang in there for the duration, becoming complacent, and restarting with a vengeance. Perhaps, it is better to have a goal of improving health markers, keeping a checklist of selected healthy foods at portion sizes eaten daily, and exercising. In addition, portion sizes and calories county. Plus, slow and steady wins the race.

But then for her to get her dream of finding her mate only to have it kind of crushed was hard to read in parts. She really tries so hard to put on a good front, but you know it’s hard for her.As for Clark, I wanted to be mad at him. I wanted to be so annoyed that he wasn’t on board and by default was inherently hurting Misty. text: This tale commits one major "flaw." And these jumps are long, often occurring in overlapping timelines and extremely convoluted. It was clear that the author wanted to write a mystery but rather than work it around one character, tries to use multiple conflicting characters to help blur the storyline and path.That never works for me anymore. I dislike it when long established authors like David Weber does it, even when he has the experience to make the characters in the scene work. Here, the characters did not work. They were too unformed, and I quickly lost any interest.It might be a great book, but I just couldn't tolerate the focus jumps, so once again I have to give it 2 stars. title: Is Your Job Important?
text: Does your job seem fulfilling? Or, to put it more clearly, do you feel your job has a net positive value to society as opposed to just a way to make money? If your answer is no, or if you think a larger percentage of the world’s jobs fall under the low- value umbrella, then you might like this bookWhat this book proposes is that far too many jobs are of this variety. The individual working the job could quit tomorrow and nothing significantly negative would happen to the company he/she works for, or society at large. Far too many people are engaged in pointless employment, or so this book suggests, which raises the important question: Why is this happening in a capitalistic society, one that is supposed to strive toward efficiency with very few exceptions? The book attempts to answer that question, and others related to it, as it rambles on for nearly 300 pages.As I read this book, I started to think about jobs I have held and others have held that fit the definition of this type of job. I can think one job of my own, from the past, that came close, but it still wouldn’t qualify. However, I can think of positions others have held that do, indeed, fit the definition. And it does make me wonder why the folks in charge allowed such a situation to occur.This book does raise some interesting questions and it does get you thinking about the usefulness of employment. It makes you wonder why the workweek hasn’t been shortened and remains at 40 hours, at least here in the United States. It makes you wonder about the push for job creation by politicians of most every stripe and whether or not this push has, in some way, encouraged the proliferation of so many useless job positions. And it makes you wonder why someone with a do- nothing job wouldn’t enjoy it at least for the easy money, since we are so often told that most anyone will slack if given the opportunity.I like any book that brings up thought- provoking questions and this book accomplishes exactly that. But it is not without its flaws, chief among them the fact that the book presents an idea without any formal research. It’s an idea that, while intriguing, has no official research to back it up. Another issue I have is the books repetition. It continues to repeat similar thoughts over and over. The book could have been reduced about one hundred pages and easily gotten its message across. And then, there are the estimations that book makes about b.s. jobs and their occurrence. I find it hard to believe that roughly one- third of all jobs qualify as useless. I can agree that most any job has its moments of uselessness and that most of us could finish our necessary tasks in fewer hours at work each day. But based on my own observation, I cannot see how so many jobs fall under the b.s designation.Our free- market economy thrives on competition and the efficiency that is supposed to result. Capitalism is still the best system around for wealth creation and opportunity, but it is not without its flaws, and the same could be said for any other economic system. There are certainly useless jobs all around the world, and this book is a good way to at least get you thinking about these jobs, why they exist, and what it means for society. I have issues with this book, but it is still an interesting enough read to recommend.

title: sweet and cute
text: This is a book that came my way through social media, let’s face it, I’m a sucker for a decent 1 minutes long video. It’s basically marketed as a second chance romance with a sports flair and some cheating in the past.I’m not a ready who doesn’t like cheating, in fact I love reading it, so this doesn’t bother me at all, but i know for a lot of readers it’s a hard time. You do see some of the cheating behavior in scenes that take place in the past, so if that’s not your thing, there ya go.So you have Poppy and Keir who seem to be basically college sweethearts and Keir goes into pro football and she stays behind in college, but they maintain a long distance relationship. Of course it doesn’t work out. I’m not spoiling anything, this is all very up front and takes place in the past.I like second chance romances for a couple of reasons. 1) the grovel (especially in cheating situations) 2) the emotional upheaval (I like a good cry) and of course 3) the payoff when they finally figure it all out and come together.So the grovel. Keir acknowledges it was wrong. Straight up not excuses. Thank god. I hate excuses. He also tries his best to prove himself to Poppy in the present, backs off when he can tell Poppy is all up in her feels. He does seem like a good guy. A moron when his dreams came true and he became a hot shot pro footballer, but he’s a very different guy years later.Emotional upheaval is really on the part of Poppy. I mean I feel for her. Does she open herself up to being hurt again? I don’t honestly love how her best friend keeps trying to push them back together without checking in first, if she had checked in first I would be a lot more okay with it. But she does it without checking and Poppy is clearly uncomfortable early on. She’s a really sweet girl, and I liked her, but I don’t know that I was overly invested in the trajectory of the relationship. I wanted to be. I just didn’t get there. Honestly I think some of my issue was the whole thing was sweet. They were a sweet couple working out their issues in this sweet/cute manner on sweet/cute dates. Sweets fine but I like soul crushing lol!The payoff was nice. Overall, I think they are cute. It was a quick read for me. I think this would be a really good palate cleanser, it’s not overly emotionally, but the story kept my attention and the characters are likable so overall, it worked out.

title: How Radio Caught the Killer
text: In 1910, the North London Cellar Murder was as much as a news event as the O.J. Simpson trial in the 1990s and the Kennedy assassination in 1963. The difference was that it happened on the cusp of another technological marvel, the birth of wireless communication—and it was wireless communication that finally trapped the alleged murderer.Dr. Hawley Crippen was an American homeopath who basically sold patent medicines in the US, and later in London. Infatuated with a blowsy young woman named Cora who wished to become a musical performer, he married her. From all accounts he was a gentle, indulgent husband who bought his wife a huge wardrobe, supported her career even though she wasn't that talented, and didn't seem to mind her having a supposedly non-sexual relationship with a fellow male performer, Bruce Miller. Cora later changed her stage name to Belle Ellmore, and it was under that name she disappeared. Crippen initially told everyone that she'd gone home to America to nurse an ailing relative, had gotten sick herself, and died, to cover up the fact, he confessed, that she had run away to the US with Miller. By this time Crippen was being unfaithful with his secretary, Ethel Neave. The police had no reason to doubt his story, until Crippen and Neave left town and someone started poking at the bricks in the cellar.As in DEVIL IN THE WHITE CITY, Larson tells Crippen's story parallel with Guglielmo Marconi's efforts to transmit wireless telegraph signals. Marconi, a driven, spoiled man with an Italian father and Irish mother, had read about Hertz's discovery of electromagnetic waves, and, not really understanding them, pressed on with inventions that transmitted them, and was convinced that these waves could carry telegraph signals "through the ether." At the time transatlantic cables could carry messages from land to land stations, but ships at sea had to rely on passing ships to tell them news or flares to signal distress. Marconi's massive wireless stations, with their blue sparks and thunderclap sounds, would revolutionize communication with ships. But he faced stiff competition with British scientist Oliver Lodge and scientist and magician Nevil Maskelyne, among others, who also had been working on Hertz's "waves," but in a less aggressive fashion, and who considered Marconi a foreign interloper with an unproven system.As always with Larson, well written, but if you're in this for the true crime stuff (Crippen's was the second most famous British murder case, after Jack the Ripper), the Marconi stuff will bore you, and if you're in it for the science, the Crippen portrayal of a disintegrating marriage will probably make your eyes glaze over. There's also a great deal of Marconi's legal disputes with Lodge, Maskelyne, and even people he's recruited to help him, like Forrest. But there's also a great deal to like in the Marconi parts, especially the portraits of early wireless telegraphy stations—the blue sparks and the crackling of the early transmitters sound at once both frightening and fascinating—and the weather they battled against. Enjoyed, but you must have patience with it.

title: Samsung 32 Art TV
text: I am going to provide a list of pros and cons... but to summarize, I am really disappointed. The most disappointing thing... a HUGE BLACK box that you must use. They "say" it can be flush mounted to the wall - but NOT without a giant black brick below it. There are multiple photos in the ads of the TV "in use" but not a single one that shows that ugly black box!!! Here are my thoughts...PRO... (and they are weak)- A fairly good picture.- Mediocre sound.- The art option - which is also on the con - so it kinda wipes this one out. You chose a piece and it will stay on for up to 4 hours. There is a setting to adjust 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours.- The best "pro"? The white frame was easily installed (it has magnets- but the little plastic pieces to secure the outer plastic to the frame are SUPER hard to secure. Good luck. I have provided a large number of photos to show all that I am outlining.- It's a smart TV - which means you can hook up to your wifi and watch your netflix, prime, hulu, disney+.... but I will say I had to login my "samsung acct" in order to "load" my Amazon prime. Really? Just more ways for Samsung to follow you - you have to agree to them tracking/tracing you. GRRRR... I should move this to the con list... another pro/con that wipe each other out.CONS....- First and foremost - that UGLY black box. Approximately 9"x4"x1 1/2" . You cannot use the tv without it. The power cord plugs into it. If you planned on flush mounting (which is included with the TV - the most complicated and awful install imaginable) you will have an ugly black box under the TV.- We had to purchase an adjustable frame to mount to the wall in order to hide the black box behind it. AND a white power cord so that the "showing" cord is at least white. I may hire an electrician to put a plug in behind it but at this point you have to wonder how much more I will spend to make this work as the photos all show. GRRRR- The remote. Good luck getting the back open to put the batteries in!! It doesn't just "slide" open as the only direction on this is printed on the remote - and arrow pointing to the end of the remote. If you find yourself with one of these TVs - here's a hint... get a dime. Gently work into the top where the red plastic (the infrared tip) and the white body of the remote... wiggle it - ever so gently - back and forth... We eventually got it open. Sheesh.- We attached the ugly black box to the back of the TV which means we had to install the pull away mount to have room to do that. So NO flush mount - which I was really looking forward to.- The art.... very pretty. You get to see ONE - You MUST sign up, with a credit card, for a 31 day free trial to see any others. It also will not allow you add your own photos unless you sign up. It costs $4.99 a month after the trial. There are a lot of art options - but is it worth $4.99. I am on the fence. Because it doesn't "look" as I was lead to believe it would look like - a flush mounted frame.- Overall, I am hugely disappointed. The ads are very, very misleading. You will find in the official description the mention of a "mini box"... which the black box clearly is not - "mini" in anyway.Also, you should know that if you purchase an adjustable wall mounting kit, you will likely need to alter it to fit. We had to rig with TWO mounting sets to make it work - The arms were not long enough. We also tried a larger kit but it showed beyond the edges of the frame even though the mounting kit was meant for a 32" TV. Eh.For those that are curious - this TV is manufactured in Mexico.I would recommend looking for something else - unless you're cool with the ugly black box, a monthly fee for art and a lot of cord dangle. We did make the choice to keep it - for now. The thought of trying to repack it was overwhelming. And in all honesty, we had NO IDEA how much we were going to have to go through to make this work. If we could have seen into the future, we would have taken the 3 hours to repack and return it. Live and learn. I really hope our experience can help others avoid our mistake!

Laurent is quite happy to be vintner living in the Provence but Maggie still would prefer to return to Atlanta and her life as an advertising copywriter. When her best friend, Grace, announces that she and her family are returning to the States Maggie is more convinced that ever that she will never be happy in France. Once again though Maggie becomes involved in assisting the police to solve a murder and of course, endangers herself in the process.This novel, like the rest of the series, has a great deal of promise. text: Oh, what a STUPID main character.Yes, another review and another main character who I felt needs to have his skull checked to see if there is a brain in his head. I'm beginning to wonder why so many authors just can't write about an intelligent man when they write these still fantasy tales about the harem they wish they could have. (I wonder if they ever consider the fact that they write main characters who are over-sexed, buffoons is why no girl wants them.)Sorry, that was unfair, but it does fit my feelings when reading this book. The MC starts out as a failure and a drunk, who supposedly failed out of some military boot camp partly due to his drinking his life away, but due to some back room politics ends up on a special scouting mission with a female trainee who feels an obligation to him because he stopped a bully early on in the boot camp. And of course, he sobers up for her (not that he had a choice there was no alcohol around.) And discovers that on the new continent he's visiting females with power need a male to Bond to, and he soon has multiple women of power bonding to him as he stumbles through a number of intrigues and set pieces.Honestly, the action isn't bad, although the villains have less brains than the main character, which I would have though impossible. But that's a product of some truly bizarre world building that definitely didn't meet my, "could this happen in real life" standard by a huge margin. Its just inconceivable to me that Leo believes his world makes sense.Its not a bad tale overall, but with the horrible start and an MC who should never have been written about, I found that the action and plot (and yes, there is a plot, huzzah!) couldn't completely redeem the story. I can give this 3 stars. Some people are going to like this especially with the sex scenes (honestly, if I want to read sex scenes I know where to find true erotica, not the watered down teenage fantasies in books like this.) But I read for plot and character. Plot we do have here, character..... not so much.

text: I must admit that watching anime series that have a decent amount of fan service is a guilty habit. I can't say its exactly a pleasure because you can have a series like High School of the Dead where the fanservice manages to be both excessive and fun in an otherwise rather dramatic and serious series, but then you get anime series where the fan service becomes cringe inducing and the characters are nauseating. For me this usually means that you have a typical harem comedy lead with less brains than your average rock and angst levels that would eclipse the sun.Sadly, this series falls hard into the second category. The MC is a teenager at home alone when the naked (of course she's naked) catgirl appears in the pantry, and said MC freaks out completely. (and completely predictably if you know how your average American male teenager views harem comedy anime.)And it never got better. I disliked the MC, and found the catgirl to have less personality than Barbie (and she's a plastic doll.). We got high levels of angst (I can't let my parents see this catgirl). Low levels of thought, and no clear plot definition early on, which just left this story stuck at the starting gate.It's not a bad idea, but there needed to be a serious consideration of character and plot to give this story a direction that could hook me. title: Its a normal tale for this author, but that doesn't mean its bad.
text: I knew what I was getting when I started reading this series. Jan likes his heroes to be a bit over-powered, his female sidekicks to be very oversexed and the plot itself to be surprisingly simple under a layer of misdirection that doesn't hold up to much if any scrutiny.But that doesn't make his stories bad. Just a bit predictable with a plot that will plod along at a rather consistent pace. This book was exactly that. There is nothing special here. His earlier series with Sean the were-lion had many of the same elements as this tale, only told over a longer period as that series eventually ran 24 books, and this series was clearly plotted to end much faster. That merely means there are fewer girls, a weaker villain and simpler obstacles.Its still a good read. I'm not sure I'd recommend it to everyone, but I can say I'd recommend it to most.
